per_claim_limit.rationale: coverage.per_claim_limit (5,000) is the ceiling for a single claim, except that a category whose own sub_limit is higher (dental 10,000, diagnostic 10,000, pharmacy 15,000, alternative_medicine 8,000) is governed by that higher sub_limit. The ceiling is compared against the policy-eligible amount (after line-item exclusions and pre-auth rejections, capped at the claimed amount), excluding pre-authorised items, whose amount is governed by the pre-authorisation itself. This is the only reading consistent with all ground-truth cases: TC008 (consultation 7,500 > 5,000 -> REJECTED), TC006 (dental 12,000 billed, 8,000 eligible <= 10,000 -> PARTIAL 8,000), TC010 (4,500 <= 5,000). It replaces the v1 hand-picked category list, which was internally inconsistent (pharmacy has the largest sub_limit yet was capped at 5,000).

document_type_descriptions.PRESCRIPTION: doctor's prescription (with the doctor's name, registration number, diagnosis and signature)
document_type_descriptions.HOSPITAL_BILL: hospital bill or clinic invoice (itemised charges, bill number and the total amount paid)
document_type_descriptions.PHARMACY_BILL: pharmacy bill (medicine names, quantities and the net amount paid)
document_type_descriptions.LAB_REPORT: lab / diagnostic test report (test names and results, signed by the pathologist or radiologist)
document_type_descriptions.DENTAL_REPORT: dental report or treatment notes from your dentist

assumptions.sub_limit: opd_categories.*.sub_limit is used as the per-claim ceiling only where it exceeds coverage.per_claim_limit (see per_claim_limit.rationale). Where it is lower (consultation: 2,000) it cannot be a hard cap on the payable amount — TC010's ground truth approves 3,240 — so it is surfaced as a non-blocking WARN for the reviewer instead of a guess.
assumptions.annual_limits: coverage.annual_opd_limit is applied per patient; coverage.family_floater.combined_limit is applied across the employee's family. Year-to-date paid amounts come from ClaimSubmission.ytd_claims_amount when the caller supplies it, otherwise from the claim store's approved amounts within the policy year. The larger of the two is used so a caller cannot understate usage.
assumptions.submission_deadline: Checked against ClaimSubmission.submission_date. The upload endpoint stamps the server date; the JSON API accepts it explicitly. When absent the rule is logged NOT_EVALUABLE (visible in the trace) instead of silently passing.
assumptions.coverage_start: A dependent's coverage (and waiting periods) start on their own join_date if present, otherwise the primary member's join_date, otherwise the policy start date.
assumptions.pre_existing_conditions: waiting_periods.pre_existing_conditions_days (365) is not enforced: telling a pre-existing condition from a new diagnosis needs medical history this system does not receive. Logged NOT_EVALUABLE on every claim.
assumptions.pre_auth_validity: pre_authorization.validity_days cannot be checked without the pre-auth issue date; any supplied pre_auth_id is treated as valid and logged as such.
assumptions.branded_drugs: Pharmacy line items flagged is_branded=true by extraction get branded_drug_copay_percent; items with unknown brand status get the base copay_percent and a WARN.
assumptions.exclusion_precedence: A permanent exclusion supersedes a waiting period for the same condition (TC012: obesity is both excluded and has a 365-day wait; telling the member they become eligible later would be false).
assumptions.per_item_pre_auth: Pre-authorisation is evaluated per bill line item using that item's amount, so a covered consultation on the same bill is still paid when an MRI on it is rejected. With no itemised bill, the prescription's tests plus the claimed amount are used.
assumptions.fraud_history: Caller-supplied claims_history is merged with the claim store (union by claim_id), never used instead of it, so a caller cannot evade frequency checks by sending an empty history.
assumptions.fixture_documents: Documents carrying pre_extracted_data (the eval fixtures) are trusted as the extraction output ONLY when ALLOW_FIXTURE_DOCUMENTS=true; otherwise the API rejects them with 422, because a caller could otherwise skip extraction and submit invented amounts and diagnoses. The eval harness and the test-case runner enable it for their own runs.
assumptions.clinical_coding: Conditions are matched by whole-phrase keywords (interpretation.json) on the diagnosis and treatment. The vision model also proposes condition_tags from a closed vocabulary generated from policy_terms.json (specific waiting-period conditions and exclusion names). A keyword match can reject; a model tag WITHOUT a keyword match only routes the claim to manual review (CLINICAL_CODING_UNCERTAIN), so an LLM inference alone never denies a claim.
assumptions.readability: A document the model reads as POOR, or with illegible fields, keeps its own extraction confidence and adds an explicit 'partially_unreadable' confidence factor to the trace, so the reason for the lower score is visible.
assumptions.negation: A condition keyword preceded, within negation_window_words words of the same clause, by a negation cue (negation_cues) is not treated as a diagnosis: 'No family history of diabetes' does not trigger the diabetes waiting period. Negated matches are listed in the trace evidence. Abbreviations are expanded in place so the cue still applies.
assumptions.extraction_confidence: For live extractions the document's confidence is computed, not taken from the model: extraction_model_weight x model-reported confidence + (1 - extraction_model_weight) x completeness, where completeness is the share of extraction_critical_fields present for the detected document type. Both inputs are logged. Readability problems are a separate, visible confidence factor (partially_unreadable). Fixture documents keep their stated confidence.
assumptions.minimum_evidence: A live extraction that is readable but has none of extraction_minimum_evidence for its type (e.g. a prescription with no patient name, diagnosis or treatment) is returned to the member as unusable instead of being adjudicated on empty data.
assumptions.diagnosis_required: For categories that require a prescription, a claim with no readable diagnosis or treatment cannot be checked for exclusions or waiting periods, so it goes to manual review (DIAGNOSIS_UNREADABLE) rather than being approved.
